title: Multi-setup machining: carry the machined stock (rest body) from one setup into the next

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## Summary

Machine a part in several setups (flip, re-clamp, rotate on a vise or fixture) where **each setup starts from the material the previous setup left** - the in-process stock ("rest body") - instead of from a fresh block. Today every setup machines, verifies and computes rest against its own declared block.

## What exists today (verified in the code)

- **Multiple setups shipped in M3.2 A** (RECOMMENDED.md "M3.2 A - Multiple setups", commit `33f5658`): `SetupDef {stock, wcs, datum_from}`, `ActiveSetup`, `CreateSetup` / `DeleteSetup` / `ActivateSetup` / `SetOperationSetup` (`crates/app/src/commands/setup.rs`), per-setup lazily spawned stock and WCS furniture (`"Setup2/Stock"`, `"Setup2/G54"`), datum transfer that clones the source's stock snap and WCS, program order rank-then-name, per-setup tool lists and setup sheets.
- **The flip transform was never built.** M3.2 A deferred it: "Placement is the flip; the transform is M3.3 ... Rotation/flip matrices deliberately do not exist yet." M3.3 shipped posts and machine definitions instead; `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` still says "the flip transform between setups is M3.3's engine".
- **The program sim only CLIPS between setups** (`stock_sim::simulate_document` -> `clip_to_setup_stock`): one world-frame dexel grid; entering a new setup lowers columns to at most the new block's top and never moves what the previous setup cut. A re-clamped face reads as leftover (conservative, never a gouge) - but a **rotated or from-model stock in a later setup refuses the sim outright**.
- **Rest is same-setup only**: `rest::prior_digest` / `rest::prior_state` (`crates/app/src/rest.rs`) skip operations of other setups, so a setup-2 roughing op re-cuts air where setup 1 already removed material.

## Goal

A later setup inherits the previous setup's machined stock, transformed by the re-fixturing (flip/rotation/translation), as its starting stock - for generation (rest-aware strategies skip air), for verification (gouge/rest/rapid laws judge the real material) and for display.

## Open questions (need research and decisions before breakdown)

1. **Representation of the carried body.** Dexel columns are frame-bound (Z-up grids); a flip needs re-sampling. Options: carry the field/SDF engine's volume and re-sample in the new frame; extract the machined mesh (dual contouring, #23) and re-voxelise it; or the B-rep kernel route once Solidcore lands (#27, booleans). Accuracy vs. cost vs. memory for each.
2. **Transform model.** Where does the setup-to-setup transform come from - the WCS datums (datum transfer), a picked face/edge (3-2-1 alignment, #187), a fixture definition (M3.2 B fixtures)? Is it rigid only (flip/rotate/translate) - yes for now; any tolerance on re-clamping?
3. **Interaction with existing laws.** The implicit-setup law (zero setups = legacy), the conservative CLIP law (keep as fallback?), rotated/from-model stock refusal, stamps/digests (a setup-1 regenerate must mark setup-2 ops Stale), program order.
4. **Rest across setups.** `rest::prior_*` must read the carried body; which ops consume it (adaptive, pocket, 3D rough, rest machining)?
5. **Lathe / mill-turn.** Second-op on the sub-spindle or a part flip on a lathe - same mechanism, or separate?
6. **Fixtures and collision.** The fixture solid (M3.2 B) changes per setup; collision checks must use the carried stock plus the new fixture.
7. **UI.** Showing the incoming stock per setup, choosing "start from previous setup" vs. "new block" per setup (a user parameter with a default), setup sheets.
8. **Performance.** Re-sampling a large machined body on every setup change; caching per setup.
9. **Prior art** (public documentation only, per the Clean-Room Protocol): how CAM systems describe "in-process stock" / "stock from previous setup" behaviour to users.

## Proposed breakdown (file these as sub-issues once researched)

- [ ] Research note: carried-body representation and re-sampling cost (dexel vs. field vs. mesh vs. B-rep)
- [ ] Setup-to-setup rigid transform: definition from datums / alignment, stored on the setup, undoable
- [ ] Program sim: carry the machined body into the next setup through the transform (replace or extend the CLIP law; keep refusal where it cannot judge)
- [ ] Rest across setups: `rest::prior_*` read the carried body; stamps/digests mark downstream setups Stale
- [ ] Generation: rest-aware ops in a later setup start from the carried body
- [ ] Verification: gouge / rapid / hidden-rest laws judge against the carried body
- [ ] UI: per-setup "start from previous setup" option (default on for setup 2+?), incoming-stock display
- [ ] Lathe / mill-turn second operation
- [ ] Fixture collision with carried stock

## Done means

Every sub-issue filed, linked here and closed; then this umbrella closes (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

Related: #23 (machined mesh), #26 (dexel retirement), #27 (Solidcore), #45 (setup navigation and ordering), #187 (3-2-1 WCS alignment), #196 (WCS per setup).
